question: In a nuclear reactor, fast neutrons are produced during fission but a moderator is placed around the fuel. Why is a moderator necessary for a sustained controlled reaction?

options.A: It absorbs all neutrons so that no more fissions take place.
options.B: It slows down fast neutrons by collisions without absorbing them appreciably. Slow neutrons are more effective at producing further fissions, helping sustain a controlled chain reaction.
options.C: It supplies high-energy neutrons to start fusion in the fuel.
options.D: It converts neutron energy directly into electrical energy.
